surfaces.part: ATM header panel (white/grey face with blue stripe)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 14 px wide for rows 0-29, with no ellipse and no widening or narrowing. Rows 1-4 are a light header band, but it runs straight into the dark row 5 and a blue stripe at row 6. That makes it a vertical face with no front-edge line or eave shadow. The rest is stacked vertical faces: the screen and housing at rows 10-19 and the keypad panel at rows 20-28. Nothing shows a horizontal surface seen from above, and no opening or contents are visible. This is a flat front elevation of a vending-style machine, not an open container.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small ATM with only 13 distinct colours in total. Its body ramp has about 4 lightness steps (white-grey top, light, mid, dark), against 5-6 on the stall, well and hedge. The measured facts show 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, and the picture shows a uniform dark outline around the whole silhouette and the screen, the 'sticker' look. The references with material-toned outlines (hedge 0%, stall 1%) have no such line. Only the crook lamp, a thin pole, is as neutral. The 12 visible tones per tile and 0% flat coverage keep it from being flat, and the keypad dots and screen add some detail. It is still thinner and more outlined than the stall and well, which have 17-20 tones per tile with tinted edges. Without the density numbers against it, the neutral outline and shallow ramp still make it read flatter than the references.

surfaces.part: ATM header panel (white upper face with blue stripe)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 14 px wide from row 0 to row 29, with no widening or narrowing, so there is no ellipse. The light rows 1-4 lead straight into a blue stripe at rows 5-7 and read as a front-facing header panel. There is no front-edge line followed by eave shadow, so no horizontal surface is drawn. Below that are a screen with a bezel (rows 11-17) and a keypad panel (rows 20-28), all seen face-on. There is no opening and no visible contents, so it is not an open container. It is a flat front elevation of an ATM.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ATM is a small grey-blue kiosk with a screen, a keypad and a card slot. Its body is built from only about 3 lightness steps (light panel, mid body, dark edge), where Beodeul props such as the well and cheese stall use 5-6. The outline is a neutral, nearly colourless dark line: the measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 100%, against 0-1% on the tinted hedge and cheese-stall references (the lamp-crook also reads 100%, but it is a thin metal pole). It looks like the sticker-style edge rather than a dark tone of the neighbouring material. Visible tones per tile are 12, which is above the hedge (9) but below the well (20) and stall (17), so density is a little lower. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, but the keypad and screen detail is sparse, and the body panels are smooth with little grain or speckle. Overall it is clean but shallower than the references, with a neutral outline and few shading steps.
